(A) WHAT IT IS: the REACH inequality of rings_below_4.md s.1. A wall of side s between two corner crowds of
the flat + tilted type (flat meeter at offset delta from its wall, TILT-MIN partner of tilt theta) is
spanned in contact with k = 0 wall squares iff 2 + R >= s, R(theta, delta) = cos + sin + delta - (delta -
sin theta) tan theta; the gap for a third member is s - 2 - R < 1.
Blue: the least-waste crowd (delta = sin theta + 0.02) -- it bridges s only for theta >= theta* = 30.3 / 33.8 /
36.0 deg at s = 3.88 / 3.95 / 3.99 (the PI's "fairly high tilt"); purple: the deep-offset crowd (delta =
0.98) bridges every s < 3.98 at any tilt but wastes the corner (A'); orange / green: the extent cos + sin
and A231's chord 1/max(cos, sin) of one tilted square for comparison. 0.00 s.

(A') WHAT IT IS: the k = 0 CONTACT curve: at side s the flat meeter's offset delta that makes R(theta, delta) =
s - 2 (solid), for the tilts where TILT-MIN allows it (sin theta + 0.02 <= delta < 1); dashed: the
uncoverable area of that crowd in its corner (A237's sandwich census in a side-6 box) -- the dichotomy: a
low tilt needs delta near 1 (the corner strip is wasted), the least waste sits at the high-tilt end theta*.
Read with (A): below 4 a two-per-wall ring in wall-to-wall contact exists at every s in (3, 4) along this
curve; what it cannot do is balance (page 3, D). 0.00 s.
fits
(B) WHAT IT IS: A226's crowd ring at S = 3.90, eps = 0.02 (one_flush.md s.3.4): at each corner the flush corner
square lifted eps up its wall (flat, orange) and its neighbour tilted eps/2 = 0.57 deg hovering eps/4 above
the wall with a vertex poked under it; a RATTLER crowd: the only contacts are the four flat squares' walls,
no square touches another.
ring: 8 squares, pattern 2 2 2 2 (meeters per corner BL BR TR TL), 8 contact rows; free FJ LP (walls +
contacts, no floor, no crowd rows): INFEASIBLE; minimal external load closing the balance: 1.000;
torque-only: infeasible (the forces cannot close around the ring).
RED = the deficit rows drawn at the squares that need them (external force at the centre, torque as an arc): 0:
torque only; 1: interior; 2: torque only; 3: interior; 4: torque only; 5: interior; 6: into ceil; 7:
interior.
